sent_subject: Sprout & Stitch: three fast fixes and a landing‑page plan to test this week
sent:
Amrita —

A tight teardown from a fresh look at sproutandstitch.example this morning, focused on what moves first orders fastest.

Fix now (under 90 minutes)
- Character rendering: £ and dashes are showing as odd symbols in nav/cards — fix the encoding site‑wide; it quietly dents trust.
- Put delivery + free returns right beside Add to bag on product pages (not just in bars/footers) to remove last‑second hesitation.
- Make “new” actually read as new: sort newest‑first on Home and New In; add a small “Added this week” badge.

Build this week (promise‑led, not homepage‑led)
- Create three landing pages and point ads/emails to them:
  1) Rain‑Ready — coats + layers; one CTA; tight grid.
  2) Knee‑Proof — reinforced bottoms; proof up top (close‑up knees, short copy).
  3) Under £20 — gift‑friendly picks; price‑forward; quick add.
- One ad, one promise, one page. In our audits, homepages lose about half of paid traffic in the first five seconds.

Keep ads efficient
- We retire most creative after about three weeks of falling click‑through. Not three weeks from launch.
- Every concept should ship with at least three variants so the account can learn which one works. On Glow Theory, a phone photo beat a £12k studio shoot.
- Oatside Kitchen saw cost per first order down 38% after moving ads off the homepage onto three offer pages; in that test, the plainest page won.

Measure it
- Judge by add‑to‑bag and first‑order rate versus your Home baseline; don’t let click‑throughs decide.
